title: Stored x-only leaf birthday search on secp256k1 at 125.072641020980: six leaves per batched inverse, a two-fraction class label with a lattice mass bound, metered rare-carry branches and k-record block messages with tbz slot tests, fwd tbz, k256 d46 and every record's delivery charged

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold stored-leaf birthday search of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.390000001 over the challenge and fresh algorithm coins, with no heuristic: the Chen-Stein method on cross-node leaf pairs bounds P(no collision), and drops, caps, wrong class indices, label errors and the enumerated carry sites of the kernels (section 3.4) are charged failure rows, as are the caps of two meters, while RNDR, the ideal coin source, adds none (section 6, in success.md). On every run its total work is at most 2^125.072641020980 target-group-operation equivalents (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit). Each pair of generator points X, Y gives six leaves, the x-coordinates of phi^t(X) + Y and phi^t(X) - Y for t = 0, 1, 2, from one batched inverse of y_Y^2 - y_X^2 (section 3.1). A class's label is the top 100 bits of the fractions v*/p and (beta v* mod p)/p, v* = min(x, beta x, beta^2 x); each leaf computes its x's three fractions (within 68 below, and within [-1, 70], at 128 bits) and KEY's index j picks the pair (j, j + 1): 41 instructions for j = 0 and 46 for j = 1, 2 (section 3.3). A wrong index (rate below 2^-54.29 per leaf) and a label error near a block boundary (below 2^-19.8) are charged missed-collision rows; no leaf is dropped. A lattice count from secp256k1's Frobenius bounds a box of label values at 1 + 2^-19 times its share, so classes sharing the 182 matched bits give false candidates charged to the caps. Machine (section 2.1): 2^72 nodes, each with one processor (base AArch64 with FEAT_RNG and FEAT_LSE) and a memory below 2^64 bytes; a port has a message block for one-record messages and, per destination, a record block of k = 256 slots whose header store makes a k-record message; links deliver a message's data at the address its sender stored and keep no flags, rings or counters. At each hop every message is charged its delivery as route.s code, dlv (6) or dlvk (4k + 2 = 1026, per record the two LDPs and two STPs of dlv), which the experiment executes for every message, and its port's in-flight count (2). The sender's emit (7 at hop 1; h2s 7.25 at hop 2) writes each record into its destination's block, and a flush (8) sends a full block at its cursor or drops it; as a pair slot holds a multiple of k records, a block is kept or dropped whole, and the records kept, their order and the final cursors equal those of sending each record alone (section 4). Hop 1, hop 2 and grouping are charged 7 + 1036/256, 7.25 + 1036/256 and 14.546875 per record (scan_ranges: 195/64 per record, at most 25 per d4 range and 8 per candidate). The rare carries and borrows of the field macros are taken by a branch over a fixup that completes the chain, so every result is bit-identical to an inline chain; a node starts a batch only while its fixups are at most 2^45 - 43 q2, so the ledger charges 4*2^45 per node and Markov's inequality charges the cap. certificate.py gives at most 323.8039 instructions per leaf and the claim 125.072641020980. Peak memory at most 2^135.9989 bytes; preprocessing at most 2^108.1047 units, included; no advice; certificate.py checks that the work, memory and preprocessing figures are the least 12-decimal (work) or 4-decimal values at or above their exact values, and that 0.390000001 is below the success bound. The bound is for the machine of section 2.1. Lineage: our round-6 package (tighter candidate cap and j slack, on the round-5 base); new here: scan_ranges dispatch index by one UBFX (25 per d4 range) and the phase-4 exchange at its itemization; no prior acceptance or score is a premise. This is an analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the six-leaf kernels on production points, with every emitted label of a leaf outside KEY's window set and D against its class's label, and the class-label test; run the emit, both hops (each message delivered by executing dlv or dlvk) and the grouping on a 4 x 4 machine, and the record blocks on every path (machine.py), against exact references; check the arithmetic sites and rare-carry fixups of section 3.4 (sites.py); compare every kernel's counts with certificate.py; run the q25 toy (toy.py) and certificate.py. Budget-limited parts run stated minimums. Not a production-scale attack.
